title: sp-4.6 "next frame's field is paper" reads frame 930, which the 70-frame morph puts in the middle of its line phase
text: The recipe `{kind: xsheet, field: world, expect: equals, value: crayon, at: next}` reads the exposure sheet's world on the frame after the story point's last (930). The crossing from the frame to the art world is declared 895-965 (`timeline.crossings`: length 70, split 35/35 around the cut at 930), so the sheet reads `home>crayon/line` on 930 and `crayon` only from 965. The morph cannot end by 930 without the crossing becoming a 35-frame one (the cut at 930 would be its last frame) or starting at 860, inside sp-4.5; with the 70-frame morph a story point that ends at 930 can only read 'crayon' on 965 or later. Options: read the world 'after the crossing' (`at: after-crossing`, the first frame whose world is a plain world), read it on 965, or move the story point's end to the crossing's end. Beat 4's other line of the point, 'outside luminance falls >= 50 %', is met by the staging (the frame's light wells wide as she nears it and narrows as she steps through, `emitter.at` in v3/blocking/the-frame.json): 40.7 on 899 and 14.3 on 929 (-65 %). Ruled by the director in the screenplay: sp-4.6's third recipe now reads the field at the crossing's end (f965), not the next frame.
after: the recipe reads the first frame the crossing has finished, or the crossing ends on 930
